rules: 44/44 Acts source ranges have nonempty source verse entries in all 3 Catholic transcriptions, but 2 original reference endpoints are absent. Their absence is NOT permission to synthesize an extra verse.
Chronology is biblical Acts order; appended Pentecost scene 182 is reviewed, but its research-array index is not narrative time.
Acts 14:20-28 must be edition-mapped through verse 27 in these sources, and Acts 19:23-41 through verse 40; printed-edition re-collation required.
No unsupported ancient ship tracks, apostolic itineraries, shoreline landing points or historic room coordinates created.
Overlapping scene excerpts and stage-by-stage narrative segments do not introduce duplicate canonical Atlas events.
Biblical topography, family identity, scene literary acceptance and publication are separate research stages.

reviewedRows.title: The road to Damascus
reviewedRows.existingLocationClaim: Damascus region · not exact roadside location
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Acts 9:1-9 records Saul nearing Damascus, but not a precise road bend, chapel or point of encounter.

reviewedRows.title: Ananias baptises Saul
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Acts 9:10-19 names Damascus and the street called Straight; modern traditional house identifications require independent evidence.

reviewedRows.title: Saul escapes Damascus
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Acts 9:20-25 recounts escape in a basket over the wall; it does not certify the preserved chapel/window location.

reviewedRows.title: Saul visits Jerusalem
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Acts 9:26-30 names Jerusalem; no authenticated meeting room or exact travel path is given.

reviewedRows.title: The disciples at Antioch
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Acts 11:19-26 names Antioch and disciples first called Christians there; it gives no specific church/house address.

reviewedRows.title: Barnabas and Saul are sent
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Acts 13:1-3 names Antioch and the Spirit's commissioning; exact gathering room or modern building is not identified.

reviewedRows.title: Departure from Seleucia
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Acts 13:4 names Seleucia as departure port; not an exact embarkation pier or vessel.

reviewedRows.title: Salamis on Cyprus
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Acts 13:5 names Salamis and synagogues; the specific first-century synagogue locations are not identified.

reviewedRows.title: The mission to Cyprus
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Acts 13:4-12 traverses Seleucia/Salamis and reaches Paphos. A single pin at Paphos cannot represent the whole Cyprus mission.

reviewedRows.title: Perga in Pamphylia
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Acts 13:13-14 names Perga and then Antioch in Pisidia; treat as successive named towns, not one event point.

reviewedRows.title: Antioch in Pisidia
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Acts 13:14-43 describes preaching at Antioch in Pisidia; exact synagogue building or podium is not certified.

reviewedRows.title: Iconium resists the preaching
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Acts 14:1-7 names Iconium and departure into Lycaonian cities; no precise preaching room, mob location or ancient route.

reviewedRows.title: Lystra and the miracle
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Acts 14:8-20 locates the healing and ensuing hostility at Lystra; modern settlement/site and exact stoning spot are not established.

reviewedRows.title: Derbe and the return
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Acts 14:20-28 describes Derbe and reverse visits through Lystra, Iconium, Antioch and Perga; not a single Derbe incident. Verse 14:28 is absent from the three imported research witnesses.

reviewedRows.title: Council in Jerusalem
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Acts 15:1-29 recounts the council but names no authenticated meeting chamber. Keep the apostolic decree distinct from a modern location.

reviewedRows.title: A second departure
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Acts 15:36-41 describes the Paul/Barnabas disagreement and separate journeys; do not map both parties as one continuous route.

reviewedRows.title: Timothy joins the mission
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Acts 16:1-5 names Derbe and Lystra; exact initial meeting point is not given and Timothy's family identity needs the proper named source.

reviewedRows.title: The Macedonian vision
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Acts 16:6-10 includes movement across Phrygia/Mysia and the Troas vision; it gives no particular modern dream room or berth.

reviewedRows.title: The crossing to Macedonia
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Acts 16:8-12 includes Troas, Samothrace, Neapolis and Philippi as separate named stages. Map point sequence is textual, not certified ancient sailing geometry.

reviewedRows.title: Landfall at Neapolis
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Acts 16:11-12 names Neapolis and onward Philippi; no specific historic landing pier or ancient road trace is established.

reviewedRows.title: Lydia and the church at Philippi
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Acts 16:11-15 places Lydia's encounter beside a river outside Philippi; exact riverbank prayer spot or baptistry identification requires external evidence.

reviewedRows.title: Paul and Silas in prison
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Acts 16:16-40 narrates beating, prison and the jailer's conversion; a modern identified prison chamber is not proven by the text.

reviewedRows.title: Paul at Thessalonica
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Acts 17:1-9 names Thessalonica and Jason's house, but not a certified contemporary house or synagogue structure.

reviewedRows.title: The believers at Berea
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Acts 17:10-15 names Berea and its hearers but no exact ancient synagogue location or route.

reviewedRows.title: The Areopagus at Athens
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Acts 17:16-34 names Athens and the Areopagus, but the speech's exact architectural position versus institution is a separate historical question.

reviewedRows.title: Corinth and the tentmakers
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Acts 18:1-18 covers tentmaking, synagogue teaching and Gallio's tribunal. No shop or hearing space coordinates are certified by the passage.

reviewedRows.title: The mission returns to Antioch
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Acts 18:18-23 spans Cenchreae, Ephesus, Caesarea, Jerusalem and Antioch, then the next departure; Antioch alone cannot represent the entire passage.

reviewedRows.title: Paul revisits Galatia and Phrygia
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Acts 18:23 names the Galatian country and Phrygia but **does not name Pisidian Antioch**. Existing scene 165's location claim requires correction/qualification.

reviewedRows.title: The mission in Ephesus
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Acts 19:1-20 names Ephesus but spans baptisms, synagogue and lecture venue without proving extant specific interiors.

reviewedRows.title: Riot of the silversmiths
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Acts 19:23-41 is one longer than the installed witnesses' Acts 19:23-40. The latter conclude at 19:40. No missing verse may be invented; exact riot assembly location remains archaeological review.

reviewedRows.title: Eutychus restored at Troas
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Acts 20:7-12 names the Troas gathering and upper room, but does not establish the modern building address or floor level.

reviewedRows.title: Farewell at Miletus
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Acts 20:17-38 identifies Paul's farewell at Miletus and summoned Ephesian elders, without an exact site of speech or shoreline.

reviewedRows.title: Paul arrives at Tyre
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Acts 21:1-6 places the group in Tyre, including prayers at the shore. This does not authenticate a modern dock or route pin.

reviewedRows.title: Prophecy at Caesarea
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Acts 21:8-14 names Caesarea and Philip's house, but the location of that house and the prophetic action remains unknown.

reviewedRows.title: Paul arrested at the Temple
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Acts 21:27-36 names the Temple and barracks stairs as narrative contexts, without certifying a modern precise stair or room.

reviewedRows.title: Before Felix at Caesarea
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Acts 24:1-27 records the hearing before Felix at Caesarea; no exact contemporary tribunal room can be sourced from the passage.

reviewedRows.title: Paul appeals to Caesar
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Acts 25:1-12 spans Festus in Jerusalem and Caesarea for the hearing and appeal. It must not collapse both places into a single courtroom.

reviewedRows.title: The long voyage from Caesarea
reviewedRows.existingLocationClaim: Crete · island region, not vessel position
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Acts 27:1-12 begins with departure and traces several maritime stages before Crete, not only Crete. Ancient nautical positions are not reconstructible from the narrative.

reviewedRows.title: A storm on the sea
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Acts 27:13-44 narrates a storm at sea without an independently proved contemporary vessel track or landing GIS point; the canonical Atlas explicitly avoids a fabricated shipwreck location.

reviewedRows.title: Shipwreck and hospitality on Malta
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Acts 28:1 identifies Malta, but does not certify today's named St Paul's Bay, beach or any individual footprint as the shipwreck landing point.

reviewedRows.title: Syracuse and Puteoli
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Acts 28:11-14 lists Syracuse, Rhegium and Puteoli as consecutive Mediterranean and mainland stops; the specific ship berths remain uncertain.

reviewedRows.title: The Italian mainland
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Acts 28:13-14 is a short subsection of scene 178 Acts 28:11-14. Do not create a second Italian-mainland arrival event from the overlap.

reviewedRows.title: Paul arrives in Rome
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Acts 28:16-31 records Rome and Paul's preaching but does not narrate his martyrdom, death or site. Never append fabricated events after the final canonical reading.

reviewedRows.title: Pentecost: the Holy Spirit descends
reviewedRows.existingLocationClaim: Jerusalem · city context; the precise room is not identified by Acts 2
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Acts 2:1-41 narrates the Spirit's descent and Peter's preaching without proving that an extant Upper Room was the precise place; keep appended scene 182 in its correct theological order following Ascension.
